title: Narrow-mode surface reflow
description:
Objective: finish spec section 4.16 below the shell — the per-surface narrow reflow that the shell task's narrow mode makes drivable.

Scope, all measured on disk:
- DECISION-BUTTON PINNING. approval-detail-plan.tsx:146 already stamps a data-pinned="true" marker, but grep for data-pinned across *.css returns 0 hits: nothing targets it. Add the stylesheet rule behind the existing marker; do not invent a second marker.
- ROW FIELD-SET PARITY. Section 4.16 says tables drop to two-line rows with "no column removed, only reflowed". There is no table, thead, tbody or role=grid anywhere in the app (0 hits), and the two table surfaces section 4.16 implies (section 4.11 Runs/leases, section 4.12 Resources) do not exist: cr.runs and cr.resources are both 0 hits. What DOES exist is li/div row surfaces. The assertable form is field-set equality wide versus narrow on those rows. "Two-line" itself is a pixel property and is NOT checkable in this harness.
- BOARD REMAINDER. board-layout.css:50 already carries the narrow block (sticky cr.board.columnjump, overflow-x auto plus scroll-snap on cr.board.columns, 85vw snap columns) and board-surface.tsx:209 renders the column-jump control. Only the gaps left after the shell task land are in scope. Do not rebuild what is there.
- LOCK AMENDMENTS. Any file added under a frozen directory requires amending goals-board-ban.test.ts's readdirSync array, and any new import into board-surface requires amending its frozen import allowlist. Amend deliberately and narrowly; never widen a lock beyond the file being added.

NOT IN SCOPE: the width ladder, the width-derived hook, the narrow marker, the nav rail, the `?` overlay and the inspector sheet (all owned by task-3e3275476efe4e9086a2a89b7c78cab0). The graph clause and the Runs/Resources table clause are permanently out — see the DoD not-applicable item.

Owned paths: apps/control-room/src/board/**, apps/control-room/src/approvals/**, and the row surfaces named in the plan. NOT owned: apps/control-room/src/a11y/**, apps/control-room/src/shell/**, apps/control-room/src/performance/**.

Hard dependencies: Narrow-mode source of truth and shell reflow (task-3e3275476efe4e9086a2a89b7c78cab0) must reach DONE first — the parity assertions need its narrow render mode to have a narrow root to compare against.

Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test
definitionOfDone: A stylesheet rule targets the EXISTING data-pinned marker at approval-detail-plan.tsx:146 so decision buttons pin at narrow width, and a source-text pin asserts the rule exists. No second marker attribute is introduced. The rule's visual effect is explicitly NOT asserted — jsdom evaluates no CSS.

Row field-set parity is asserted across every row surface the plan names: the set of field test-ids rendered inside a row at narrow width equals the set rendered wide, with each set asserted non-empty first so the comparison cannot pass vacuously. This is the assertable form of "no column removed, only reflowed".

Every stylesheet this task adds or edits carries a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block, and a source-text pin asserts it. Without this the reduced-motion guarantee that board-layout.css:68 currently provides silently regresses as soon as a second stylesheet exists.

Any amendment to the frozen readdirSync arrays or the frozen import allowlist in goals-board-ban.test.ts names exactly the files added and nothing more, and the amended test still fails when an unlisted file is introduced — verified by adding a scratch file, confirming red, and removing it.

Recorded as explicit not-applicable WITH the reason, never as a passing assertion over zero cases: section 4.16's table clause against Runs and Resources (cr.runs and cr.resources are 0 hits — those surfaces do not exist), and section 4.16's graph clause (three committed tests ban the cr.graph. prefix).
pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test passes, and each new failure-path test is verified by mutating the production surface and confirming it goes red.
taskRails: Pinned UI spec: D:/projexts/moes/docs/plans/2026-08-05-moe-v1-control-room-spec.md SHA-256 C55AF8A9FC7386E6492FD57E34A4B8321ABAAE4E4E08FF38703544B58B0BEF1F. Section 4.16 is lines 425-433.

THE HARNESS CANNOT SEE LAYOUT — measured, not assumed. offsetWidth, clientWidth and getBoundingClientRect().width are all 0 even with an inline width, and document.styleSheets.length is 0 because Vitest stubs the CSS import. Never assert that a button reached the viewport bottom, that a row wrapped to two lines, or that a media query evaluated. Those are source-text pins or nothing.

Do not add a motion ban that fights the board. board-layout.css legitimately uses scroll-snap-type and scroll-snap-align for section 4.16's column behavior. Any motion guard must target animation, transition and @keyframes and scroll-behavior:smooth — never scroll-snap.
Do not edit apps/control-room/src/a11y/** or apps/control-room/src/shell/**. Those belong to task-ab8c9489ab6446c384e977a3e1cc8063 and task-3e3275476efe4e9086a2a89b7c78cab0 respectively.

The standalone control room displays daemon truth and nextAllowedCommands; it never derives authority, readiness, or evidence strength. Narrow mode is presentation only: it may never change which commands exist, which actions are enabled, or any truth class.
Keep each production file below 400 lines, target 250. Explicit owned paths only; no git add -A.

implementationPlan.description: GATE CHECK, and stop here if it fails. Confirm task-3e3275476 (Narrow-mode source of truth and shell reflow) is DONE and its narrow substrate exists on disk: a width ladder/classifier, a width-derived hook driven by window.innerWidth plus a resize Event, and a narrow marker attribute on cr.shell.root. Locate these by NAME with grep — do NOT copy identifiers out of any plan document, because those symbols were designed but not yet built when this plan was written. If the substrate is absent, report blocked rather than inventing a narrow mode; every parity assertion below is vacuous without a real narrow root. While here, re-check two premises that may have expired: (a) whether cr.runs and cr.resources now exist, since task-ddb3bf77 is building them — if they do, DoD 5's table-clause not-applicable is STALE and the clause becomes applicable; (b) that spec 4.16 clause 3 is still complete on the board (board-layout.css:14 overflow-x, :26 sticky headings, :50 the 959px block, board-surface.tsx:209 column-jump). Confirm no directory this task touches is frozen: approvals and a11y appear in no *-ban.test.ts. No files are modified.
implementationPlan.note:
GATE CHECK RUN AND IT FAILS. No files modified. Per the step's own instruction ("stop here if it fails... report blocked rather than inventing a narrow mode"), proceeding to report_blocked.

DEPENDENCY IS NOT DONE. task-3e3275476efe4e9086a2a89b7c78cab0 is status WORKING at 3/10 steps, actively being implemented by another worker right now.

THE SUBSTRATE IS HALF-LANDED, AND THE HALF THAT MATTERS IS THE MISSING ONE. This is the distinction that decides the block, so I measured both sides rather than reading the status alone:
- PRESENT: `apps/control-room/src/shell/viewport.ts` landed at 12:47 (that task's step 3) and exports `ViewportMode` ("COMFORTABLE" | "FUNCTIONAL" | "NARROW"), `VIEWPORT_WIDTH_LADDER`, `classifyViewportWidth`, `useViewportMode`, plus a `ViewportRefusalReason` of "INVALID_VIEWPORT_WIDTH".
- ABSENT: nothing CONSUMES it. `grep "viewport|narrow|Narrow" apps/control-room/src/shell/frame.tsx` returns exactly one hit, a comment at :84 about narrowing commands to one kind — unrelated. `cr.shell.root` renders at frame.tsx:211 as `<div data-testid="cr.shell.root" ref={keyboard.rootRef}>` with no narrow marker and no viewport import.

So a width ladder and a hook exist, but there is NO NARROW RENDER MODE. Rendering the shell at a narrow width today produces a tree identical to the wide one. Every field-set parity assertion in steps 4-5 would compare a tree against itself and pass — the vacuous-sweep defect this plan's own risk #1 names, arriving dressed as a green suite. A hook that nobody calls is not a narrow root.

Wiring it myself is not available: `apps/control-room/src/shell/**` is explicitly NOT this task's owned path (task rail 4), it belongs to task-3e3275476, and that worker is mid-flight in it. Editing it would be both a scope violation and a live collision.

TWO PREMISES RE-CHECKED AS THE STEP REQUIRES, both still hold:
(a) DoD 5's table-clause not-applicable is STILL TRUE, not stale. `grep -rc "cr\.runs|cr\.resources" apps/control-room/src` returns zero files with any hits, so task-ddb3bf77 has not landed those surfaces. The not-applicable may be carried forward with its reason intact — but it must be re-measured again at completion time, not inherited from this note.
(b) The `data-pinned` marker is real and still unique: `approval-detail-plan.tsx:146` renders `<div data-pinned="true" data-testid="cr.approvals.detail.actions">`, and the only other occurrence in the repo is the assertion at `approval-details.test.tsx:218`. Nothing in any stylesheet targets it. The production gap the plan identified is genuine and unchanged.

WHAT IS INDEPENDENTLY PLANNABLE TODAY, flagged so the block does not read as "nothing here is doable". Steps 2-3 — the approvals stylesheet targeting the existing `data-pinned` marker, its `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block, and the source-text pins — need NO narrow render mode at all. They are pure source-text assertions in `apps/control-room/src/approvals/**`, an unfrozen directory, and they close DoD 1 and DoD 3. Only DoD 2 (field-set parity) is gated on the dependency.

I did not do them anyway, deliberately: this task cannot complete without DoD 2 regardless, and landing a partial commit in a shared worktree while the dependency's owner is mid-flight buys nothing and adds a collision surface. If an architect would rather have DoD 1/3 now, that is a clean separate task and I will take it — it is roughly one stylesheet, one bare import and one test file.

implementationPlan.description: TDD red: write the failing source-text pin for the decision-button pinning rule. Following the established pattern at board/goals-board-ban.test.ts:134-156, read the real stylesheet file, assert a non-trivial length and one known selector FIRST so the pins cannot pass vacuously, then assert it targets the EXISTING data-pinned marker and carries its own @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block. Also assert the file contains no display:none, visibility:hidden, overflow:hidden or text-overflow:ellipsis, since spec 4.16 forbids removing anything at narrow width. Label every assertion in this file as a source-text pin, not behaviour — jsdom evaluates no CSS. The test fails because the stylesheet does not exist.

Make step 2 green. Add the approvals stylesheet with a narrow-width rule that pins the decision buttons, targeting the EXISTING data-pinned="true" marker at approval-detail-plan.tsx:146 — do not introduce a second marker attribute, and do not modify the JSX marker itself. Include a @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) block; board-layout.css:68 has one today and a second stylesheet without one silently degrades that guarantee. Any motion suppression targets animation, transition, @keyframes and scroll-behavior:smooth only — never scroll-snap, which board-layout.css uses legitimately. Wire the sheet with a bare import in approval-detail-plan.tsx, mirroring how board-surface.tsx:9 imports board-layout.css. src/approvals/ is not frozen by any ban test, so no listing or allowlist amendment is needed.

TDD red: write the failing cross-surface narrow parity sweep, the assertable form of spec 4.16's "no column removed, only reflowed". For each row surface, render it inside the shell at a wide width and again at a narrow width using the real substrate from step 1, and assert the set of field test-ids rendered INSIDE a row is equal between the two. Cover the surfaces that exist: cr.goals.row.* (goals-home.tsx:104), cr.timeline.row.* (timeline-row.tsx:141,:173), cr.review.row.* (attempts/review-surface.tsx:80), cr.provenance.row.* (shell/provenance-panel.tsx:26), plus the list surfaces approval-inbox (cr.approvals.pending) and reconciliation-inventory (cr.health.reconciliation.list), whose items are li elements rather than .row. ids. Add the board's clause-3 remainder here too: the cr.board.card.* and cr.fact.* id sets are identical wide and narrow, which is "card content unchanged". Non-vacuity is mandatory and is the whole point: assert the surface list is non-empty, assert it covers each surface exactly once, and assert each id set is non-empty BEFORE comparing — two empty sets are equal, so a sweep that rendered nothing would otherwise pass while testing nothing. If this file approaches 250 lines, split the fixtures into a sibling module rather than letting it grow.

Make step 4 green with the MINIMUM production change, and be honest about how much that is. Fix only what the sweep actually reports: a field that disappears at narrow width, or a row whose id set differs. It is a legitimate and likely outcome that some or all surfaces already reflow correctly and need no change at all — in that case record 'measured, no production change required' explicitly in the step note and keep the sweep as the regression guard. Do NOT invent a stylesheet, a wrapper, or a refactor to make the task look substantial; and do NOT weaken the sweep to make a real failure disappear. Any surface that does need a fix and lives in a FROZEN directory (goals, timeline, recovery) must be fixed by editing an existing file, never by adding one — adding a file there turns its ban test red by design.

Verify the locks are untouched and still biting. This task should require NO amendment to any *-ban.test.ts, because every file it adds lands in approvals or a11y, neither of which is frozen. Confirm that: run board/goals-board-ban.test.ts, data/data-ban.test.ts, evidence/evidence-timeline-ban.test.ts and recovery/recovery-import-ban.test.ts and confirm all four are green with no diff to any of them. Then prove the relevant one still bites rather than assuming it — temporarily add a scratch file to src/board/, confirm goals-board-ban goes red, and remove it. If you did have to amend a lock, that is a signal a file went in the wrong directory: move the file rather than widening the lock, since a widened allowlist that was never needed is a permanent hole.

Verification. Run the single gating command: pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test. Capture fresh output verbatim as completion evidence; do not reuse an earlier run. Confirm the committed suites that touch this area are still green — approvals/approval-details.test.tsx (whose :213-220 DOM-order assertion covers 4.16 clause 5's first half), the a11y ui-wide acceptance tests, and shell/gating-keyboard.test.tsx. Then satisfy epic rail 6's mutation requirement, which a green suite cannot demonstrate on its own: mutate, confirm red, revert. At minimum mutate (a) the data-pinned selector in the new stylesheet so the source-text pin goes red, (b) the reduced-motion block, deleting it to confirm that pin bites, and (c) one rendered field on one row surface so the parity sweep goes red — this last one is the important drill, because it proves the sweep is comparing real content rather than two empty sets. Record which mutations ran and that each produced red. Attribute any repo-wide red by path: this task owns apps/control-room/src/approvals/** and the new a11y test only.

Adversarial self-review before complete_task. Read the diff as an attacker. Check: does the parity sweep compare two EMPTY id sets anywhere, and does it fail when a surface renders nothing; does it actually enter narrow mode using the real substrate from task-3e3275476, or has it silently compared a tree against itself; does any assertion claim something jsdom cannot see — that a button reached the viewport bottom, that a row wrapped to two lines, that a media query evaluated; does the new stylesheet carry its own prefers-reduced-motion block, and does any motion guard wrongly forbid scroll-snap; was a second data-pinned-style marker introduced when one already existed; did any file land in a frozen directory, and was any ban test amended that did not need to be; is DoD 5's table-clause not-applicable still TRUE at completion time, or did task-ddb3bf77 land cr.runs and cr.resources and make it stale; is every file under 250 lines; and are there any debug, probe, scratch or generated evidence files left in the commit. Finally, state plainly in the completion note how much production code this task actually changed — if the answer is 'one stylesheet and one import', say so rather than implying more.

1. DO NOT START UNTIL task-3e3275476 IS DONE. Its narrow render mode is the only way to obtain a narrow root; without it every parity assertion in this task compares a tree against itself and passes while testing nothing. That is the vacuous-sweep defect, dressed as a green suite.

2. BIND TO WHAT SHIPPED, NOT TO WHAT I PLANNED. The viewport hook, ladder constants and narrow marker were designed in task-3e3275476's plan but do not exist on disk today. Locate them by NAME at step 1 and use the real exports. Do not copy identifiers out of this plan or that one — a plan is not disk.

3. A DoD ITEM MAY BE SATISFIED WITH NO PRODUCTION CHANGE, and that must be REPORTED, not silently enjoyed. If the row field-set parity sweep passes first time, the correct outcome is 'measured, no change required' recorded explicitly, with the test kept as the regression guard. Quietly shipping a green test and implying work was done is the dishonesty the epic rails exist to prevent.

4. DoD 5's not-applicable REASON MAY GO STALE MID-FLIGHT. It says the table clause is N/A because Runs and Resources do not exist. task-ddb3bf776f5245f49a3422105001b665 is now creating exactly those surfaces. RE-CHECK at step 1: if cr.runs and cr.resources exist by then, the table clause is APPLICABLE and must be handled, not copied forward as N/A. Do not inherit a not-applicable whose premise has expired.

5. DO NOT AMEND A LOCK YOU DID NOT NEED TO TOUCH. Every file here lands in an unfrozen directory. If you find yourself editing goals-board-ban.test.ts, stop — you have put a file in the wrong place. A widened allowlist that was never needed is a permanent hole.

6. THE PINNING RULE'S EFFECT IS UNASSERTABLE. jsdom evaluates no CSS and document.styleSheets.length is 0 because Vitest stubs the import. Never assert that a button reached the viewport bottom. The rule is pinned as source text and labelled as such.

7. NEVER BAN scroll-snap in a motion guard. board-layout.css legitimately uses scroll-snap-type and scroll-snap-align for spec 4.16 column behaviour.
